exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Credentials in Registry
exploitedBy.relevance: Unauthenticated access to a registry can expose credentials stored within it, making this the most directly relevant technique.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Query Registry
exploitedBy.relevance: Unauthenticated registry access enables adversaries to query the registry for sensitive configuration and credential information.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Additional Cloud Roles
exploitedBy.relevance: Overly permissive push authorization reflects excessive cloud role assignments that allow unauthorized parties to push images.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Additional Container Cluster Roles
exploitedBy.relevance: Excessive push permissions map directly to container cluster role abuse, enabling adversaries to introduce malicious images.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Code Signing Policy Modification
exploitedBy.relevance: Disabling image signing and verification is analogous to subverting code signing policies, allowing unsigned or malicious images to run.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Invalid Code Signature
exploitedBy.relevance: Without signing enforcement, adversaries can deploy images with invalid or absent signatures to masquerade as legitimate content.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Credentials In Files
exploitedBy.relevance: Secrets embedded in image layers are stored as files within those layers, directly matching credentials-in-files exposure.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Private Keys
exploitedBy.relevance: Private keys are a common type of secret embedded in container image layers, representing a high-value credential exposure.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Implant Internal Image
exploitedBy.relevance: Adversaries can implant images containing embedded secrets to persist access or exfiltrate credentials via the registry.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Build Image on Host
exploitedBy.relevance: Lack of scanning integration allows adversaries to build and push vulnerable images that evade detection.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Escape to Host
exploitedBy.relevance: Unscanned images may contain vulnerabilities that enable container escape to the host system.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Additional Cloud Credentials
exploitedBy.relevance: Weak or shared service account credentials can be leveraged to add or escalate cloud credentials for persistent access.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Steal Application Access Token
exploitedBy.relevance: Shared service account tokens are prime targets for theft, enabling adversaries to authenticate as the service account.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Application Access Token
exploitedBy.relevance: Weak service account credentials may result in token reuse or theft, allowing adversaries to use application access tokens for lateral movement.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Software Deployment Tools
exploitedBy.relevance: An unrestricted network-exposed registry acts like a deployment tool accessible to adversaries for pushing or pulling malicious images.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Data from Cloud Storage
exploitedBy.relevance: Unencrypted backend storage allows adversaries to directly access and exfiltrate image data from cloud storage buckets.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exfiltration to Cloud Storage
exploitedBy.relevance: Unencrypted storage facilitates exfiltration of sensitive image layers or embedded secrets to external cloud storage.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Services Registry Permissions Weakness
exploitedBy.relevance: Insufficient logging fails to detect permission weaknesses being exploited within registry services.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Malicious Image
exploitedBy.relevance: Mutable tags allow adversaries to silently replace legitimate images with malicious ones, causing users to execute malicious content.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Patch System Image
exploitedBy.relevance: Tag mutability enables adversaries to patch or replace system images without detection, similar to system image patching attacks.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Lifecycle-Triggered Deletion
exploitedBy.relevance: Missing retention policies mean lifecycle-triggered deletion controls are absent, leaving stale or sensitive data indefinitely accessible.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
exploitedBy.relevance: Excessive host privileges on the registry process can be abused to establish persistence via run keys or startup mechanisms.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
exploitedBy.relevance: Unpatched registry software is directly exploitable as a public-facing application, allowing remote code execution or unauthorized access.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
exploitedBy.relevance: Known vulnerabilities in unpatched registry software can be exploited to escalate privileges on the host system.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Vulnerabilities
exploitedBy.relevance: Adversaries can acquire or leverage known vulnerabilities in unpatched registry software to plan and execute attacks.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Brute Force
exploitedBy.relevance: Without pull rate limiting, adversaries can perform brute force attacks against the registry authentication mechanisms without throttling.
